quantity: descendant-tolerant cross-entropy on the Stage 1b nesting graph
status: NOT BUILT - blocked by section 7 gap 2 (H2)
reason: the design says outright: do not rely on the descendant-tolerant loss until nesting is re-tested. Stage 1b's nesting layer missed ALL THREE cases declared for it - nest_tcell, nest_treg, nest_tumour_ki67; two found no edge and one merged instead
note: a loss built on an untrusted parent/child graph would silently reward wrong predictions, and the failure would look like a modelling result rather than a graph defect. Stage 6 ships PLAIN targets. This is a deferral, not a rejection: re-test the nesting layer and the loss can be added without touching anything else

quantity: neighbourhood-context auxiliary loss (one of the planned four)
reason: it predicts a cell's spatial neighbourhood, which requires z_neigh from Stage 4. Stage 4 is deferred by user decision, so this loss has no input and cannot be written at all
note: THIS CHANGES THE DECLARED ABLATION. The design says 'train with 2 losses and with all 4'. Only THREE exist on the current roster: cell-type, masked-marker, VICReg. The ablation is therefore 2 vs 3 and is reported as such rather than quietly renumbered

reason: Gate 3 measured it over 5 lambdas x 5 folds and no lambda beat lambda=0; lambda<=0.03 sat inside fold noise and lambda>=0.1 was clearly worse while eroding the cohort guard from 0.775 to 0.231
note: carrying it at lambda=0 would be the same encoder with extra moving parts. If Stage 3b changes that verdict, this row is revisited and the change is dated

quantity: every auxiliary log-sigma at the last epoch minus its value at epoch 0
reason: Kendall uncertainty weighting is free to switch a loss OFF by driving its sigma up - the weight is 1/(2 sigma^2), so a runaway sigma silently deletes the term while training still looks healthy. A cap makes that visible instead of invisible
note: reported as a trajectory per auxiliary loss, not just the endpoint. The CELL-TYPE sigma is PINNED at 1.0 and not learned - noisy labels look 'uncertain' to Kendall weighting, and that is the one task that must not be switched off

quantity: minimum pairwise prototype distance at any epoch
reason: learnable prototypes can silently merge two classes. Macro-F1 over classes PRESENT IN THE TRUTH does not necessarily expose it, so the guard has to watch the prototypes directly
note: when a pair breaches the floor it is FROZEN and logged rather than the run being aborted - a merge is a finding about the label space, not necessarily a bug. Frozen pairs are listed in the report with their cluster names

quantity: agreement between the trained prototypes' nearest-cluster assignment and Stage 1b's clustering
reason: prototypes are learnable precisely so the protein data can correct Stage 1b. Where the model moved a prototype a long way, it is disagreeing with the clustering - that disagreement is a finding and is reported per cluster
note: no threshold: there is no principled prior for how much correction is right. Reported as a table of the largest movers with their cluster names, so a reviewer can judge whether the model or Stage 1b is wrong

quantity: LOCO macro-F1 with 3 losses minus LOCO macro-F1 with 2 losses
reason: the extra auxiliary losses are kept ONLY if they earn it. 2 losses = cell-type + masked-marker; 3 = plus VICReg. If VICReg does not improve validation macro-F1 it is dropped and that is reported
note: the design's word is 'keep the extra only if they improve validation macro-F1'. Scored LOCO over the 5 training cohorts with the stroma waiver honoured (D-32), the same quantity Gate 3 and Gate 7 use, so the three gates are comparable

quantity: LOCO macro-F1 of the shipped Stage 6 model minus the SAME encoder with Stage 3's plain linear head
reason: this is the row that asks whether Stage 6 earned its existence. The prototype loss, the collapse guard and the sigma weighting are the entire stage; if they do not beat a plain linear head on the same encoder, they are complexity without payment
note: the linear-head control is RE-MEASURED INSIDE THIS RUN, not read from Gate 3's report. Gate 3 ran on an 88-triple vocabulary before D-39 fixed it, so its 0.3642 is not comparable to anything produced afterwards. Same pattern as Gate 2's core-9 control (D-27): measure the baseline in the same run or the comparison changes two things at once

reason: Gate 3 found CRC to be the WORST fold at 0.2770 despite being the largest cohort with the second-richest panel, which points at class imbalance or label granularity rather than batch (H7). Stage 6's class-balanced sampling and prototype loss are the first things that could move it
note: reported per fold against Gate 3's per-fold numbers where the vocabulary allows. If CRC does not move, H7 stays open and the cause is elsewhere
